This Appeal, Coming On For Admission, This Day,
Vijaykumar A.Patil, J., Delivered The Following:
 Judgment

This appeal is filed by the claimants against the judgment and award dated 18.09.2018 passed by the Prl. Senior Civil Judge and JMFC and MACT-IX, Mudhol (hereinafter referred to as 'the Tribunal')
in MVC No.353/2016 seeking for enhancement of compensation awarded by the Tribunal.

2. Brief facts giving rise to filing of this appeal are that the legal heirs of the deceased Adiveppa @
Adavesha filed a claim petition before the Tribunal seeking compensation.

It is averred that on Smt.Bagawwa W/O Adavesh @ Adiveppa ... vs Hanamanth S/O Bhimappa Immannavar on 15 November, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/63482264/
2 20.02.2016, the said NC: 2023:KHC-D:13530-DB Adiveppa was travelling on motorcycle bearing No.KA- 48/L-6799 from Mudhol to Mahalingapur.

entities.text: Smt.Bagawwa W/O Adavesh @ Adiveppa ... vs Hanamanth S/O Bhimappa Immannavar
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: At that time, the driver of tractor and trailer bearing No.KA-48/T-0753, KA- 48/TA-1009 and KA-48/TA-1010 driven in a rash and negligent manner and dashed the motorcycle from hind side.
Due to the said impact, the back wheel of the tractor ran over the stomach of Adiveppa.

Immediately he was shifted to Government Hospital,
Mudhol and later he succumbed to the injuries.
It is further averred that the claimants have spent Rs.50,000/- towards funeral expenses.
The deceased was aged about 30 years, doing goundi work and earning Rs.25,000/- p.m.
It is also averred that the respondents No.1 and 2 being the owner and insurer of the offending vehicle are jointly and severally liable to pay the compensation.

Hence,
they have sought for compensation.
3. The respondents entered appearance before the Tribunal.

Respondent No.1 filed objections opposing the claim petition and contended that he is the owner of the NC: 2023:KHC-D:13530-DB offending vehicle and the respondent No.2 is the insurer of the said vehicle.
It is further contended that the compensation sought by the claimants is exorbitant, hence, prayed to dismiss the claim petition.
Respondent No.2 also filed objections contending that the driver of the offending vehicle was not holding valid and effective driving licence on the date of accident.
The owner of the offending vehicle has violated the policy conditions and therefore, the insurer is not liable to pay the compensation.
It is also contended that the deceased himself was responsible for the accident and the compensation claimed by the claimants is exorbitant.
Hence, sought for dismissal of the claim petition.
4. The Tribunal framed the issues and recorded the evidence of the parties.
The claimant No.1 has examined herself as P.W.1, got marked Ex.P.1 to P.6 and respondents examined R.W.1 and R.W.2 and got marked Exs.R.1 to R.10.

The Tribunal on appreciation of the material evidence on record,
awarded compensation of NC: 2023:KHC-D:13530-DB Rs.15,69,400/- along with 6% p.a. interest.
Being aggrieved by the same, the claimants are in appeal.
5. Learned counsel Sri Prashant S. Kadadevar for the appellants submits that the Tribunal has committed an error in assessing the income of the deceased at Rs.7,000/- p.m.
He further submits that the Tribunal has not awarded compensation towards loss of consortium to the children of the deceased and sought for enhancement of compensation.
6. Per contra, learned counsel Sri S.S. Koliwad submits that the compensation awarded by the Tribunal is just and proper and prays for dismissal of the appeal.
7. Having heard the learned counsel for the appellants/ claimants, learned counsel for the respondent No.2, perused the memorandum of appeal and Tribunal NC: 2023:KHC-D:13530-DB records.

The point that arises for consideration in these appeals is:
"Whether the appellants are entitled for the higher compensation?"
8.

The answer to the above point is in the affirmative for the following reasons:

entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: (a) It is not in dispute that in the accident that occurred on 20.02.2016, one Adiveppa who was travelling on the motorcycle bearing No.KA-48/L- 6799 succumbed to the injuries in the Government Hospital, Mudhol due to the rash and negligent driving of the driver of the tractor and trailer bearing No.KA-48/T-0753, KA-48/TA-1009 and KA- 48/TA-1010.
The contention of the appellant/ claimants is that the Tribunal has erred in assessing the income of the deceased at Rs.7,000/- p.m. which is required to be accepted.
Normally this Court and Lok Adalaths assess the income of the NC: 2023:KHC-D:13530-DB victim basing reliance on the notional income chart prepared by the Karnataka State Legal Services Authority.
In the instant case, the accident is of the year 2016 and hence, as per the aforesaid chart, this Court assess the income of the deceased at Rs.8,750/- p.m.

(b) The Tribunal has adopted the multiplier of 17 based on the age of the deceased and deducted 1/4th towards personal and living expenses of the deceased based on the number of dependants of the deceased, which do not call for any interference.

Hence, the claimants are entitled for compensation under the head loss of dependency as under:
Rs.8,750+3,500 (40% of Rs.8750/-) = 12,250/- Rs.12,250-3,062 (1/4th of Rs.12,250/-) = 9,188/- Rs.9,188 x 12 x 17 = 18,74,352/-

(c) The Tribunal has awarded a sum of Rs.40,000/-
towards loss of consortium only to the claimant NC: 2023:KHC-D:13530-DB No.1 who is the wife of the deceased.

However, it is settled law that the wife and children of the deceased would be entitled to Rs.40,000/- each towards spousal and parental consortium as held by the Hon'ble Apex Court in the case of Magma General Insurance Company Limited Vs Nanu Ram1.

entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text:
(d) The compensation awarded by the Tribunal towards loss of estate and towards funeral expenses is just and proper and does not call for any interference.
9.

Thus, the claimants would be entitled for modified compensation on the following heads:
 Sl.

No . Particulars Amount  1. Loss of dependency Rs. 18,74,352/-
 2. Loss of estate Rs.15,000/-
 3. Funeral expenses and Rs.15,000/-
 transportation of dead body  3. Loss of consortium Rs.1,60,000/-
 (Rs.40,000 x 4)
 Total Rs.20,64,352/-

4 10.

In view of the aforementioned, we pass the following:
ORDER (i) The appeal is allowed in part.

(ii) The judgment and award dated dated 18.09.2018 passed by the Prl. Senior Civil Judge and JMFC and MACT-IX, Mudhol in MVC No.353/2016 is modified and the claimants are entitled to total compensation Rs.20,64,352/- as against Rs.15,69,400/- awarded by the Tribunal with interest at the rate of 6% per annum from the date of claim petition till date of realization.
(iii) The respondent-Insurance Company shall deposit the enhanced compensation amount with accrued interest before the Tribunal within six weeks from the date of receipt of certified copy of this judgment.
 (iv) Apportionment, deposit and  disbursement of the enhanced  - 10 -  NC: 2023:KHC-D:13530-DB compensation shall be made as per the award of the Tribunal.
(v) Draw modified award accordingly.
(vi) Registry to transmit the records to the Tribunal forthwith.
(vii) No order as to costs.
